chunks: they would continue [in this state] until there would be left no unlawful act before Allah but they would make it lawful, and no pledge but they would break it,
until there would remain no house of bricks or woolen tent but their oppression would enter it, and their bad dealings would make them wretched,
till two groups of crying complainants would rise, one would cry for his religion and the other for this world,
and the help of one of you to one of them would be like the help of a slave to his master, namely when he is present he obeys him, but when the master is away he backbites him.
The highest among you in distress would be he who bears best belief about Allah.
If Allah grants you safety accept it, and if you are put in trouble endure it,
because surely “(good) result is for the God-fearing.”

key_terms.الْعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ: the end/result is for the God-fearing

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Umayyad era and the recommended response to divine trials according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) outlines the progressive decay of religious integrity under the Umayyads, where the sacred becomes profane and social bonds dissolve into transactional hypocrisy. This narration serves as a diagnostic of spiritual decline, urging believers to maintain steadfastness (sabr) and trust in God (husn al-zann) amidst political turmoil, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on enduring oppression with piety as the path to ultimate victory.
